newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks, uninspired by earnings, dip at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks, uninspired by earnings, dip at midday.

text.p: U.S. stocks held lower levels in midday trading on Monday, uninspired by strong quarterly profits from market heavyweights including Coca-Cola Co and General Motors Corp.
Traders and analysts said investors remained cautious after Friday's 148-point sell-off and ahead of Tuesday's report on March retail inflation.
The Dow was down about 20 points, or 0.3 percent, at 6371. Losing issues held a two-to-one lead over gainers on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The market started out with a decent tone, trying to get a technical rally, but it failed," said James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities.
The Nasdaq composite was off about three at 1204.

Coca-Cola and General Motors, both components of the Dow industrials, posted first-quarter earnings that topped Wall Street expectations. Coca-Cola rose 1-1/4 to 55, and General Motors was flat at 53.
But traders said investors were still uneasy about rising interest rates and whether companies will be able to maintain strong earnings in the quarters ahead.
"I think the key is going to be on some of these bigger companies as they look forward past this quarter," Volk said. "The question is, does it hold up?"

Analysts said investors also appeared more concerned about rising interest rates. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 3/32, its yield rising to 7.18 percent from Friday's close at 7.17 percent.
Market players have cited the 7.25 percent level on the long bond as a key point at which bonds become significant competition for stocks.

With the Dow now down about 10 percent from its record closing high of 7085, set on March 11, and the bond yield running into technical resistance, share prices may have started to level, said Robert Robbins, market strategist at Robinson-Humphrey.
"I think we're probably finding the beginning of a bottom" in the stock market, Robbins said.

An important hurdle is the Consumer Price Index due on Tuesday. After Friday's stronger-than-expected Producer Price Index data, a fresh sign of inflation in the U.S. economy would likely send stocks and bonds reeling, analysts said.
Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony, said he thought the Dow would fall to around 6200 before the end of the current pullback.
"We're anticipating we're probably going to have to go a little lower before we can get something going on the upside," Laubscher said.
USA Waste Services Inc fell 3-1/4 to 32 after it said it was buying United Waste Systems Inc in a stock swap valued at $1.7 billion. United Waste fell five to 32-5/8.
Patriot American Hospitality Inc fell 2-1/8 to 20-1/8 after it said it agreed to acquire Wyndham Hotel Corp and 11 hotels for about $1.1 billion. Wyndham fell 1-3/4 to 27-7/8.

Shares of Novellus Systems Inc sank 20-1/4 to 55-1/8 after the chip-equipment maker said its first-quarter book-to-bill ratio fell short of one-to-one and that it may face potential financial damage from a patent infringement lawsuit. The book-to-bill ratio is a key indicator of sales trends. A ratio of one-to-one means that for every $100 of equipment shipped, $100 of new orders were booked.
